claim: A 2025 study in The Lancet Global Health by Francisco Rodríguez, Silvio Rendón and Mark Weisbrot estimated that economic sanctions imposed by the United States or the European Union were associated with about 564,000 deaths per year over 1971–2021 — more than the annual number of battle-related deaths (~106,000) and comparable to the total death toll of wars including civilian casualties. The study found the strongest effects for unilateral, economic and U.S. sanctions, with no statistically significant effect for U.N. sanctions, and children under five accounted for roughly half of the deaths.

sources.label: The Lancet Global Health — Rodríguez, Rendón & Weisbrot, “Effects of international sanctions on age-specific mortality: a cross-national panel data analysis” (2025).
